subject: general
question: In which part of the Indian Constitution are the Fundamental Rights explained?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Part III**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Part III of the Indian Constitution deals with Fundamental Rights, which are enshrined in Articles 12 to 35.
 
• Fundamental Rights are meant to protect the citizens from any arbitrary actions by the state and ensure personal freedoms.
 
• These rights are enforceable by the courts, subject to certain restrictions, and are a crucial part of the democratic framework of India.
 
• Key rights include the Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV):**

 
 
• These principles, enshrined in Articles 36 to 51, guide the state in making policies and laws aimed at establishing a just society.
 
• They are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by the courts.
 
• They cover various aspects such as social welfare, economic welfare, legal and administrative reforms, and international peace and security.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Duties (Part IVA):**
 
 
• Added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, these duties are listed in Article 51A and are applicable to all citizens of India.
 
• They emphasize respect for the Constitution, national symbols, and promote harmony and spirit of common brotherhood.
 
 
 
• **Part V (Union):**
 
 
• Deals with the Union Executive, including the President, Vice-President, Council of Ministers, and the Attorney General of India.
 
• Covers the structure, powers, and functions of the Parliament and the Union Judiciary.
 
 
 
• **Part VI (States):**
 
 
• Concerns the state governments, including the Governor, State Council of Ministers, and the State Legislature.
 
• Also covers the structure, powers, and functions of the High Courts and subordinate courts in the states.
